title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 38 (Effect of refusal to accept offer of performance)

content.overview: Section 38 provides that where a promisor has made an offer of performance to the promisee, and the offer has not been accepted, the promisor is not responsible for non-performance, nor does he thereby lose his rights under the contract. Every such offer must fulfil certain conditions: (1) it must be unconditional; (2) it must be made at a proper time and place, and under such circumstances that the person to whom it is made may have a reasonable opportunity of ascertaining that the person by whom it is made is able and willing there and then to do the whole of what he is bound by his promise to do; (3) if the offer is an offer to deliver anything to the promisee, the promisee must have a reasonable opportunity of seeing that the thing offered is the thing which the promisor is bound by his promise to deliver. An offer to one of several joint promisees has the same legal consequences as an offer to all of them.
content.glance: Valid tender refused → promisor not liable for non-performance; tender must be unconditional, proper time/place, of whole obligation, with ability and willingness; offer to one joint promisee = offer to all.
content.study: A valid offer of performance (tender) that is refused discharges the promisor from responsibility for non-performance and preserves his rights under the contract. The offer must be unconditional; at a proper time and place with reasonable opportunity to ascertain ability and willingness to perform the whole; and if of goods, with opportunity to inspect. An offer to one of several joint promisees has the same effect as an offer to all. Current-law framing: test validity of the tender under the three conditions; apply discharge on refusal; note joint-promisee rule.

sections.heading: Effect of refusal
sections.body: Promisor not responsible for non-performance; does not lose rights under the contract.

sections.heading: Conditions of valid offer
sections.body: Unconditional; proper time and place with ability and willingness to do the whole; if delivery, opportunity to see the thing.

sections.heading: Joint promisees
sections.body: Offer to one of several joint promisees has the same legal consequences as an offer to all.

provisions.title: Effect of refusal to accept offer of performance

examples.title: Valid tender refused
examples.body: A offers to deliver the contracted goods at the proper time and place, able and willing. B refuses. A is not responsible for non-performance under s. 38.

hypotheticals.question: Does a conditional tender discharge the promisor?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 38 requires the offer to be unconditional.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-38
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Any offer of performance discharges the promisor if refused.
misconceptions.correction: The offer must satisfy the statutory conditions (unconditional, proper time/place, whole obligation, ability and willingness).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 38 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Test validity of the tender (three conditions). II. Confirm refusal. III. Apply discharge of promisor. IV. Apply joint-promisee rule if relevant. V. Conclude.

examTips: List the three conditions of a valid offer of performance.
